evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.105: suāvis labōrum est praeteritōrum memoria
terms.comment: What is remembered goes in the genitive. Cicero pairs the word with recordātiō: quōrum memoria et recordātiō in maximīs nostrīs gravissimīsque cūrīs jūcunda sānē fuit (Brut. 9).

terms.gloss: a recollection, a calling to mind; in the plural, memories
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: especially frequent in Cicero, in the singular and the plural.

phrases.english: sweet is the memory of labours past

phrases.latin: habet enim praeteritī dolōris sēcūra recordātiō dēlectātiōnem
phrases.english: for there is pleasure in recalling, in safety, a pain that is past

phrases.latin: cōnscientia bene āctae vītae multōrumque bene factōrum recordātiō jūcundissima est
phrases.english: the knowledge of a life well spent and the memory of many good deeds give the greatest delight
